iPadOS 27.2 is launching its beta this week, and beyond adding a redesigned Health app, Apple is bringing over a feature that recently appeared on the Mac: Siri suggestions when you select text.

iPadOS 27.2 adds the ability to bring up Siri when selecting text, just like macOS Golden Gate

Siri AI is the headlining new feature of iOS 27, iPadOS 27, and related system versions. As such, Apple has provided many different ways to invoke this completely revamped intelligent assistant.

On the iPad, you can launch Siri with the "喂 Siri" or "Hey Siri" voice command, pull down from the top of the screen, use the new Siri option in the edit menu, open the new Siri app, or use my favorite method: press CMD + Space to bring up Spotlight and then ask Siri a question inside it.

However, iPadOS 27.2 adds one more method brought over directly from the Mac.

In many situations in macOS 27 Golden Gate, when you select a passage of text, a small Siri icon appears at the top-left corner of the selection. Hover your mouse over the icon and it expands into an "Ask Siri" text input field.

iPadOS 27 doesn't have this feature. But now, as long as you connect a trackpad to your iPad, iPadOS 27.2 delivers the same effect.

As you can see from the image above, the new Siri icon starts out small and unobtrusive; just move your cursor over it and the "Ask Siri" input field appears, which is very convenient.

If no trackpad is connected, the full edit menu still appears when you select text, and you can tap Siri. But with a trackpad equipped, the whole experience is smoother and more seamless.

macOS has many similar subtle efficiency-boosting features that, though unassuming, can make everyday operations faster—it's just that iPadOS has always lacked them. So seeing recent Mac features being brought to the iPad is genuinely exciting.

What are your thoughts on the new Siri popup feature in iPadOS 27.2? Feel free to share in the comments.
